'''Anna Seigal''' is a British mathematician who conducts research in [[Algebraic geometry|applied algebraic geometry]] at [[Harvard University]] and the [[University of Oxford]]. She was awarded the 2020 [[Richard C. DiPrima Prize|SIAM Richard C. DiPrima Prize]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Richard C. DiPrima Prize |url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/major-prizes-lectures/detail/richard-c-diprima-prize |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=SIAM |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Anna Seigal awarded 2020 SIAM Richard C. DiPrima Prize {{!}} Mathematical Institute |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/35045 |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref> and the Bernard Friedman Memorial Prize in Applied Mathematics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Bernard Friedman Memorial Prize in Applied Mathematics {{!}} Department of Mathematics at University of California Berkeley |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/about/awards/grad/bernard-friedman-memorial-prize |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=math.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Seigal earned her bachelor's degree (BA honors) from [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge|Emmanuel College]], [[University of Cambridge]] in 2013, scoring 1st class, top 10 in the  [[Mathematical Tripos]]. She earned her master's degree (MMath, 2014) there earning an honours pass with distinction on Part III of the Mathematical Tripos. Her Master's essay, ''Iwasawa Theory of Elliptic Curves with Complex Multiplication,'' was supervised by [[John H. Coates]].

Seigal earned her PhD in [[Mathematics]] from [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anna Seigal - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=248708 |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref> Her dissertation, ''Structured Tensors and the Geometry of Data'',<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Structured Tensors and the Geometry of Data |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9jv5j0f4 |publisher=UC Berkeley |date=2019 |language=en |first=Anna Leah |last=Seigal}}</ref> was supervised by [[Bernd Sturmfels]]. It investigates the algebraic theory of tensors and algorithms for tensor data. At [[University of Oxford]] she is a Junior Research Fellow in [[The Queen's College, Oxford|The Queen's College]] and Hooke Research Fellow in the Mathematical Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Anna Seigal {{!}} Mathematical Institute |url=https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/anna.seigal |access-date=2022-03-12 |website=www.maths.ox.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

She was awarded the 2020 [[Richard C. DiPrima Prize|SIAM Richard C. DiPrima Prize]]<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> and the Bernard Friedman Memorial Prize in Applied Mathematics.<ref name=":2" />
